settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: doAutoCompleteJob filters candidates with i.hasPermission(Item.READ) (BuildTriggerStep.java line 151) and recurses only under that condition (lines 143-162).

Runtime scheduling resolves the item under the invoking run's ancestor context and relies on core Queue scheduling permission checks; the SECURITY-433 regression test asserts denial messages such as 'is missing the Job/Build permission', 'No item named ds found', and 'Please login to access job ds' (BuildTriggerStepTest.java lines 422-441).
doCheckJob/doCheckWait only return validation text; they do not schedule builds or modify state.
candidates.description: BuildTriggerStep.DescriptorImpl exposes Stapler-reachable methods that consume request data: doAutoCompleteJob enumerates item names (filtered by i.hasPermission(Item.READ) at line 151) across the passed ItemGroup; doCheckJob/doCheckWait resolve a caller-supplied job name via Jenkins.getActiveInstance().getItem(value, context, Item.class) and reflect existence/type in the returned FormValidation; newInstance(StaplerRequest req, JSONObject formData) reads formData's "parameter" array, looks up the referenced job with the StaplerReferer-derived context, and for each entry calls ParameterDefinition.createValue(req, jo). These are ordinary Jenkins DataBound/check/autocomplete endpoints whose access control is expected to be enforced by Stapler's Requester/ACL layer and by Jenkins' job-configuration permission checks for the surrounding build-step form. Within this repository there is no explicit permission assertion guarding these methods, and the repository does not include the calling Jelly/UI or Stapler configuration, so the effective guard cannot be confirmed from the reviewed source alone. The runtime scheduling path (step execution) is separately protected by the Item.BUILD permission enforced during queue scheduling (see BuildTriggerStepTest.permissions, lines 422-441), which reduces but does not by itself demonstrate coverage of the descriptor methods.
missing_evidence: No Stapler route table, Jelly/front-end caller, or @RequirePOST/@POST annotation is included in the reviewed files, so request-method binding and the effective Requester/ACL context for these descriptor methods could not be verified.
No source for ParameterDefinition.createValue or Jenkins.getItem/config permission enforcement is present in the repository to confirm the exact checks applied.
No runtime/HTTP test exercising these descriptor endpoints on an unauthorized user was found in this snapshot.
preconditions: An HTTP-accessible Stapler route to BuildTriggerStep.DescriptorImpl methods exists (standard for DataBound step descriptors in a Jenkins instance).
The protecting check (e.g. Jenkins.READ plus per-item Item.READ, and job-config permission for newInstance) is absent or misconfigured in the surrounding Jenkins/Stapler stack.
newInstance path requires the referenced target job to define ParameterDefinitionProperty so that createValue(req, jo) is reached (BuildTriggerStep lines 98-115).
candidates.title: Descriptor UI entry points (doAutoCompleteJob / doCheckJob / doCheckWait / newInstance) rely on external authorization not verifiable from this module

counter_evidence: The reflection is limited to a zero-argument getQuietPeriod method and only an int return type is accepted (lines 118-121), narrowing impact.
NoSuchMethodException, IllegalAccessError, IllegalArgumentException, and InvocationTargetException are already caught (lines 122-126), covering the common failure modes.
The class set reachable here is Java code already running inside Jenkins, not attacker-selected bytecode.
candidates.description: When quietPeriod is unset for a non-ParameterizedJob Queue.Task, BuildTriggerStepExecution.start reflectively invokes task.getClass().getMethod("getQuietPeriod") (line 118) and stores the result only if the return type equals int.class (lines 119-121). The catch clauses handle NoSuchMethodException (line 122), IllegalAccessError, IllegalArgumentException and InvocationTargetException (line 124). Two edge behaviors follow: (a) if a class does not declare getQuietPeriod at all, NoSuchMethodException occurs and the code silently falls through with quietPeriod still null, so the Jenkins default quiet period is used (line 128-130) — a benign best-effort outcome; (b) if the method exists but the invocation throws a subclass of java.lang.Error other than IllegalAccessError, or any other Throwable not listed, it would propagate out of start() rather than being logged, and the method's checked-exception outcome for the caller is not visible in this file. This is a robustness/error-handling observation about reflective invocation on an arbitrary class; no attacker-controlled class, deserialization, or value flow into a dangerous sink is demonstrated here, and the reflective target is code already loaded in the Jenkins JVM, not input-selected.
missing_evidence: The calling step framework's exception handling around BuildTriggerStepExecution.start was not available to confirm whether an escaping Throwable is contained.
No failing test exercises a task class whose getQuietPeriod throws an unexpected Error; the existing tests (e.g. BuildTriggerStepTest lines 279-297) do not cover this branch.
preconditions: A Queue.Task item is selected whose class exposes a getQuietPeriod method that throws an unexpected Throwable subclass at runtime, or a matching method whose access/return handling differs from the handled cases.
No explicit quietPeriod parameter is supplied to the build step, so the reflective fallback branch is taken.
candidates.title: Reflective quiet-period lookup on task class in BuildTriggerStepExecution.start: NoSuchMethodError path returns no value and ClientErrorException would escape the catch list
